ranked_evidence.title: Congo: Ebola deaths increase to over 1,000 - dw.com
ranked_evidence.snippet: 3. Skip to more DW sites. The fatality rate of the latest Ebola virus outbreak since mid-May is far higher than in previous outbreaks. The World Health Organization (WHO) on Wednesday published an overview of new data documenting the rapid spread of the current Ebola outbreak in Congo. Democratic Republic of Congo Ministry of Health data documenting cases traced between May 15 and July 19 shows that 2,473 people in Congo and neighboring Uganda have been infected by the latest Bundibugyo strain of the virus, with 999 documented deaths in Congo, and two in Uganda. The spread — the fastest ever recorded for Ebola — has continued unabated as no vaccines or treatments exist for this new strain of the virus. Health officials in Congo say some 80% of new cases have emerged through unknown transmission chains, suggesting it is spreading far faster than authorities can track. The current outbreak is in the DRC and Uganda. Skip next section More on Health from Africa.

ranked_evidence.title: Nearly 1,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo - Al Jazeera
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Nearly 1,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo. *According to WHO figures, 999 people have died in DRC and two in Uganda due to the Bundibugyo strain of the virus.*. Nearly 1,000 people have died from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the country’s health ministry says. DRC’s National Institute of Public Health said on Wednesday that 999 deaths have been confirmed since the outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of the virus began in May. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), two people have also died from the virus in neighbouring Uganda. DRC’s Health Ministry said that as of Monday, 2,473 cases had been recorded in the latest outbreak. This outbreak has killed more people at a quicker rate than any Ebola outbreak on record, including the 2013-2016 outbreak that is considered the worst on record with over 11,000 deaths out of at least 28,000 cases.

ranked_evidence.title: What experts are saying as Ebola outbreak in Congo and Uganda kills more that 1,000 people - Greenwich Time
ranked_evidence.snippet: # What experts are saying as Ebola outbreak in Congo and Uganda kills more that 1,000 people. DAKAR, Senegal (AP) — The fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history has killed more than 1,000 people in eastern Congo as health officials race to contain a virus with no approved vaccine or treatment. An update from Congo’s public ‌health ⁠institute on Wednesday said there have been 2,536 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,033 deaths, with at least 738 patients in isolation or hospitalized. The outbreak declared on May 15 is unlike most previous instances of Ebola spreading through communities because the Bundibugyo virus responsible has no approved vaccines or treatments. It is mostly concentrated in remote Ituri province, which accounts for nearly 90% of cases, but there have been others confirmed in five provinces including one of Congo’s largest cities, Kisangani, and in neighboring Uganda. The vast majority of Ebola cases are concentrated in Congo.

ranked_evidence.title: By the Numbers: This year’s Ebola outbreak has spread faster than the worst on record - San Francisco Chronicle
ranked_evidence.snippet: # By the Numbers: This year’s Ebola outbreak has spread faster than the worst on record. ABUJA, Nigeria (AP) — The Ebola outbreak in Congo has killed over 1,000 people, reaching the grim milestone nearly three times faster than the 2014-2016 Ebola epidemic that is considered the worst on record. Data from Congo’s Ministry of Health shows that as of Tuesday, the current outbreak, declared on May 15, has recorded 2,536 confirmed cases, including 1,033 deaths. This year's outbreak has reached that toll in just over two months, making it the fastest outbreak of the disease ever. According to the World Health Organization, Ebola is caused by a group of viruses, of which three are known to cause large outbreaks: Ebola virus, Sudan virus and Bundibugyo virus. Meanwhile, the Ebola virus, which is the most common out of the three, induced the 2014-2016 outbreak, considered the deadliest in Congo's history.

ranked_evidence.title: New video shows suspect shoot fireworks and pellet gun before setting fire at NYC building - NBC New York
ranked_evidence.snippet: # New video shows suspect shoot fireworks and pellet gun before setting fire at NYC building. New video shows a suspect allegedly shoot off fireworks and fire a pellet gun before pouring gasoline and lighting a large fire outside a federal office building in lower Manhattan. The new video obtained by NBC New York came from a surveillance camera that appears to capture the entire fiery attack. It begins with the suspect, 43-year-old Andrew Arrabaca, appearing to pull his cart along the sidewalk in front of the federal building at 26 Federal Plaza Monday morning. Moments later, he is seen on video igniting the fireworks and setting off numerous flares, according to officials. As the video continues, Arrabaca can be seen with what investigators said was a cannister of gasoline. He ran to the steps leading to the entrance of the federal building, pours the gasoline and a fire erupts.

ranked_evidence.title: Crazed army veteran who set fire outside NYC ICE HQ eyed other Big Apple sites first: feds - New York Post
ranked_evidence.snippet: The crazed US Army soldier who lit a raging blaze and fired a “BB rifle” outside ICE’s New York headquarters eyed other sites first for a possible “attack,” federal prosecutors said Tuesday. Andrew Arrabaca, 43, told the feds that he visited “several other sites and locations” in New York City in recent months, while carrying some of the smorgasbord of weapons police recovered from Monday’s chaotic scene, prosecutor Samantha Fry said during the vet’s first appearance in Manhattan federal court. The federal building houses ICE’s New York field office as well as immigration courts, and has become a hotbed of protests of President Trump’s deportation dragnet. Arrabaca set off fireworks, shot the pellet gun several times and was carrying a machete, two axes, a hammer and other weapons at the time of his arrest outside the building, authorities said. He was ordered held without bail on a charge of arson that carries a maximum sentence of 25 years in prison, if convicted.

ranked_evidence.title: 4 disease outbreaks making people sick this summer - Deseret News
ranked_evidence.snippet: ## Ebola, hantavirus, measles and cyclosporiasis made global headlines, too. * Four illnesses have made headlines this summer: Ebola, measles, cyclosporiasis and hantavirus. Four distinctively different illnesses have each made lots of headlines this summer: a hantavirus outbreak among passengers on a cruise ship that left folks adrift at sea for extra days and then sent some to quarantine; a measles outbreak that has featured Utah in a starring role; a nasty parasite-caused intestinal illness called cyclosporiasis that’s likely from fresh produce and an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo that has killed more than 1,000 people and infected visitors from different countries. As of July 23, no cases of Ebola disease have been confirmed in the United States because of this outbreak, according to the CDC. And the chance of it spreading to the U.S. from this outbreak is deemed to be “low.” But it continues to rage in Congo and travelers are advised not to go there at the moment.
